title: A Kindness Week
strapline: Small kind acts, all week long — and watch how they spread.
intent: A week focused on kindness makes caring for each other visible, named and celebrated across the whole room.
Noticing and doing kind things grows empathy, the heart of children's personal and social development.
Talking about how kind acts make others feel builds emotional understanding and language for feelings.
Kindness that spreads — one act sparking another — shows children they can shape how the room feels.
The week weaves kindness into everyday play, not as a lesson but as a way of being together.
implementation: Notice and name kindness out loud all week: 'That was so kind — you fetched Amir's coat when he was cold.'
Gather kind acts on a shared display — a kindness tree, jar or wall that fills up as the week goes on.
Talk about how it feels: 'How did it feel to be helped? How did it feel to help?'
Read stories about kindness and helping, and act out kind endings to squabbles and worries.
Model kindness yourself and thank children specifically, so they learn exactly what kindness looks like.
Follow the children — let them decide who to be kind to and celebrate every act, however small.
key_questions: What kind thing could you do for a friend today?
How did it feel when someone was kind to you?
How do you think that made your friend feel?
Who has been kind to you today?
How could we make someone smile right now?

impact.text: Children notice how others feel and act to help unprompted.
Children show kindness habitually and take pride in it.
Children talk about feelings — theirs and others' — and what helps.
Children resolve small conflicts with kind words.
Children help others and cooperate warmly in play.

enhancements: A kindness tree, jar or wall that fills with kind acts through the week.
Story books about kindness, helping and friendship.
A 'secret kindness' challenge — doing something kind without being asked.
Kindness cards or flowers to make and give to a friend or grown-up.
A circle-time to share and celebrate the week's kind acts.

playing_exploring: Children look for chances to be kind and enjoy the warmth it brings.
They engage with kindness stories and act out caring.
active_learning: Children keep up kind habits across the whole week.
They take real pride in helping and caring for others.
creating_thinking: Children think about how their actions make others feel.
They find their own ways to be kind and to make a friend smile.
